paras: The court-ordered whipping of seven Black boys in Taylorsville, Kentucky, took place in August 1905, when the town's police judge made a public whipping by their parents the condition of their release from jail on charges of disorderly conduct. The boys, aged twelve to eighteen, were whipped one by one before a large crowd under the town marshal's supervision, and the Louisville Courier-Journal's dispatch praised the sentence as "a good example."

According to a Taylorsville dispatch dated August 18, seven "negro boys" ranging in age from twelve to eighteen were arraigned before Judge G. B. Shindler of the Taylorsville Police Court for disorderly conduct. The dispatch does not describe the conduct behind the charge, and it names none of the boys. Shindler fined each boy $3, with the proviso that they could be released from jail if their parents would give them "a good whipping."
A large crowd gathered to watch. The parents took the boys out one at a time and, under the supervision of Marshal Jewell, subjected them to what the dispatch called "a severe castigation."
No later report on the boys, the fines, or any objection to the sentence appears in the coverage.

The only report found ran on page 3 of the Louisville Courier-Journal on August 19, 1905, among short Kentucky dispatches, under the headline "Negro Boys Convicted of Disorderly Conduct Flogged By Parents." Its opening sentence endorsed the sentence, saying that Judge Shindler "set a good example by having some young negroes whipped for disorderly conduct." No account of the episode was found in the Black press or in other white papers.

accounts.label: Taylorsville dispatch
accounts.gist: Seven Black boys convicted of disorderly conduct were fined $3 each and released from jail on condition that their parents whip them, which the parents did publicly under the marshal's supervision before a large crowd.

framing.detail: Headlined "Negro Boys Convicted of Disorderly Conduct Flogged By Parents," the dispatch opened by saying the judge "set a good example."
